traits.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Polypodiaceae and the families the Library joins to it (Dryopteridaceae, Tectariaceae, Lomariopsidaceae, Davalliaceae, Oleandraceae; most of its species are Dryopteris, Polystichum and Tectaria): Polypodiaceae proper mostly epiphytes on creeping, scaly rhizomes, fronds simple, lobed or pinnate, sometimes dimorphic, sori mostly round, no indusium; Dryopteridaceae terrestrial on erect, creeping or climbing stems, fronds once pinnate (rarely simple) to decompound, sori round with a round or shield-shaped indusium or none; Tectariaceae simple to bipinnate, indusium kidney-shaped, peltate or none; Lomariopsidaceae once pinnate, indusium round to kidney-shaped or none, fertile fronds sometimes unlike the sterile; Davalliaceae one to four times pinnate, pouch-shaped indusia; Oleandra simple, kidney-shaped indusia.

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 122, 123, family Polypodiaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 122, 123, family Polypodiaceae: rhizome habit long to short creeping, scaly; read as "short_creeping".

traits.sorus_shape.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add oblong (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 122, 123: round, oblong or elliptic.
